access_links.label: RothC download page (Fortran, Python and Windows interface)

description: RothC, the Rothamsted Carbon Model, simulates carbon cycling in soils, showing how soil organic carbon changes over time under different land use, management and climate. It is developed and maintained by Rothamsted Research in the United Kingdom through its RothC Group, which answers questions about the model and has run paid half-day training courses, paused at access. The model is generic and applied to agricultural soils worldwide in agriculture, climate change research and environmental management. The download page offers the latest Fortran code and Python code, both under the Apache 2.0 licence, and a Windows Visual Basic interface, free of charge, with previous versions on a linked page. Caveats: the page read gives no description of inputs, time step or validity range, which users must take from the model documentation and publications, and it is a single soil process model, not a whole crop model. For simulation it estimates how farm management and climate change alter soil carbon, used in climate adaptation and mitigation studies of agriculture and coupled with crop and land use models. It is related to the HWSD v2 soil database record in this catalogue, which supplies soil properties to such models.
